```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5,
                      dpi = 72, fig.align = "center")
library(WaverideR)
```

WaverideR extracts cyclic signals from stratigraphic and other time series with the
continuous wavelet transform and the superlet transform. This vignette follows a typical
cyclostratigraphic workflow on the magnetic susceptibility record of the Sullivan core
(`mag`, Pas et al., 2018): transform, test, estimate the sedimentation rate and read off the
uncertainty. The records are shortened and the resolution is reduced so that the vignette
runs in a few seconds; use the full records and finer settings (smaller `dj`, more
simulations) for real work.

## 1. Wavelet transform

`analyse_wavelet()` takes a two-column table (depth or time, value). The record is
interpolated to its median spacing, padded, and transformed with a Morlet wavelet.
`omega_nr` is the central angular frequency of the Morlet wavelet: a larger value gives a
better resolution in period and a poorer resolution in depth.

```{r wavelet}
mag_short <- mag[1:300, ]
wt <- analyse_wavelet(data = mag_short, dj = 1/12, lowerPeriod = 0.2, upperPeriod = 32,
                      verbose = FALSE, omega_nr = 8)
plot_wavelet(wt, periodlab = "Period (m)", x_lab = "depth (m)", add_avg = TRUE)
```

The shaded area outside the dome-shaped boundary is the cone of influence, where edge
effects matter.

## 2. Is a peak significant?

`wavelet_significance()` outlines the cells of the scalogram that are significant against a red
noise (AR(1)) background (Torrence and Compo, 1998) and gives the level of the global
spectrum. `method = "surrogate"` does the same with noise surrogates that pass through the
same transform, and works for superlets too.

```{r signif}
sig <- wavelet_significance(wt)
plot_wavelet(wt, periodlab = "Period (m)", x_lab = "depth (m)", add_avg = TRUE, add_signif = sig)
```

To test the power in a band, for example the precession band, use the scale-averaged
significance. It is valid for any `omega_nr`, because the null distribution is derived from the
wavelet itself rather than from a fixed constant:

```{r band}
band <- wavelet_band_significance(wt, period_range = c(0.8, 1.6), background = "ar1")
band
plot(band)
```

## 3. Superlets

Superlets combine several wavelet widths at every frequency and give a better resolution in
both period and depth. The order grows from `o[1]` at the lowest to `o[2]` at the highest
frequency. With `mult = TRUE` the i-th wavelet has `i * c1` cycles, with `mult = FALSE` it has
`c1 + i - 1` cycles (Moca et al., 2021).

```{r superlet}
sl <- analyse_superlet(mag_short, upperPeriod = 32, lowerPeriod = 0.4, Nf = 60,
                       c1 = 3, o = c(1, 4), mult = TRUE)
plot_superlet(sl, periodlab = "Period (m)", x_lab = "depth (m)")
```

## 4. Sedimentation rate from the wavelet spectrum

`flmw()` tests, for every depth and every trial sedimentation rate, how well the expected
astronomical periods (in kyr) match the peaks of the wavelet spectrum. `flmw_path()` adds
continuity along depth.

```{r flmw}
cycles <- c(2376, 1600, 1180, 696, 406, 110)   # periods in kyr
sr <- flmw(wavelet = wt, sedrate_low = 0.5, sedrate_high = 4, spacing = 0.5,
           cycles = cycles, x_lab = "depth", y_lab = "sedrate", run_random = FALSE,
           genplot = FALSE, plot_res = 2)
str(sr, max.level = 1)
```

The alternative is to sum the spectral power above a red-noise threshold. The red noise is
simulated with the autocorrelation, mean and variance of the record
(`model_red_noise_wt()`), and `sum_power_sedrate()` then scores each trial sedimentation rate
(use many more simulations in practice):

```{r sedrate}
set.seed(1)
rn <- model_red_noise_wt(wt, n_simulations = 10)
ssr <- sum_power_sedrate(red_noise = rn, wavelet = wt, percentile = 0.75,
                         sedrate_low = 0.5, sedrate_high = 4, spacing = 0.5, cycles = cycles)
dim(ssr$power_max_mat)   # trial sedimentation rates x depths
```

## 5. Uncertainty of the frequency

The Morlet wavelet has a limited frequency resolution; `wavelet_uncertainty()` gives the
conservative analytical uncertainty for the `omega_nr` used, which is the input for the
uncertainty of age models built from tracked periods.

## 6. Parallel computing and memory

Everything is sequential by default. Set `run_multicore = TRUE` (and optionally `n_cores`) in the
functions that offer it, or `options(waverider.n_cores = 2)`. The number of cores is capped by
the physical cores, the free memory and the CRAN limit, and results do not depend on it.

## References

Moca, V.V., Barbulescu, A., Nagy-Dabacan, A., Muresan, R.C. (2021). Time-frequency
super-resolution with superlets. *Nature Communications* 12, 337.

Pas, D., Hinnov, L., Day, J.E., Kodama, K., Sinnesael, M., Liu, W. (2018). Cyclostratigraphic
calibration of the Famennian stage (Late Devonian, Illinois Basin, USA). *Earth and Planetary
Science Letters* 488, 102-114.

Torrence, C. and Compo, G.P. (1998). A practical guide to wavelet analysis. *Bulletin of the
American Meteorological Society* 79, 61-78.
